chunks.text: Today, we will talk about Rwanda.
Rwanda is a green, hilly and peaceful country in East Africa.
Let's learn about it in slow and easy English.
Where is Rwanda?
Rwanda is in East Africa.
It is next to Uganda, Tanzania, Burundi and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
It does not touch the sea, but it has many lakes and hills.
It is called the Land of a Thousand Hills.
What is the capital city of Rwanda?
The capital city is Kigali.
Kigali is clean, safe and modern.
It has shops, schools, offices and hotels.
It is in the center of the country.
How many people live in Rwanda?
About 13 million people live in Rwanda.
It is a small country with a large population.
Many people live in villages, but cities are growing too.
What language do people speak in Rwanda?
People speak Kenya Rwanda, the main national language.
English, used in schools and business.
French spoken by many adults.
Swahili, used in trade and East African regions.
Many Rwandans speak two or more languages.
What is the weather like in Rwanda?
Rwanda has a mild tropical climate.
It is warm during the day and cool at night.
It has two rainy seasons.
February to May, September to November.
There is no snow and it is green all year.
The weather is good for farming.
What does Rwanda look like?
Rwanda has hills, valleys and lakes.
Volcanoes in the north.
Rain forests and national parks.
Farms, tea plantations and banana trees.
It is one of the cleanest countries in Africa.
What animals live in Rwanda?
Rwanda is famous for its mountain gorillas.
Other animals include elephants, lions and buffalo, monkeys, antelopes and zebras, hippos, crocodiles and birds.
Golden monkeys in the forest.
People visit volcanoes national park to see the gorillas.
What do people eat in Rwanda?
Rwandan food is simple, natural and healthy.
People eat bananas, sweet potatoes and cassava.
Beans, corn and vegetables.
Rice, yugali, a maize porridge and plantains.
Sometimes meat, chicken or fish.
Popular dishes, isambe cassava leaves with peanut sauce, ibihazza pumpkin with beans.
Brochettes, meat on sticks like kebabs.
What do people drink in Rwanda?
People drink water, milk, fresh or fermented, tea and coffee.
Fruit juice from passion fruit, mango or pineapple.
Adults may drink banana beer or sorghum beer.
Rwanda grows high quality coffee and tea.
What is life like in Rwanda?
Life in Rwanda is peaceful, busy and community based.
People enjoy working on farms or in small businesses, going to church or mosque, visiting family and neighbors, dancing, drumming and playing football.
Keeping the country clean.
People clean together on Umuganda Day.
What are some holidays and traditions in Rwanda?
Independence Day, July 1st.
Liberation Day, July 4th.
Umuganura Harvest Festival, Christmas and Easter.
Cuisina, baby gorilla naming ceremony.
Rwandans wear colorful clothes and traditions are passed down by storytelling and music.
Some fun facts about Rwanda.
Rwanda banned plastic bags in 2008.
Women have many leadership roles in the country.
It is one of the safest countries in Africa.
Rwanda has a national cleaning day every month.
The flag is blue, yellow and green with a sun.
Now you know many things about Rwanda.
You know where it is, what people eat and how they live.
You learned about the hills, the animals and the traditions.
Well done.
Thank you for listening to the Slow English Podcast.
I am Emily.
See you next time.
Or in King Rwanda, Mura 'beho.
